name: Chorus Before Hello
why_it_works: Most artist promos open with a pitch; this opens with the best eight seconds of the song. The ear decides in two seconds whether to stay, so leading with the chorus gives the song its only real chance, and the release date rides on a feeling already earned.

hook.pattern: Drop straight into the loudest line of the chorus, title in the first three seconds, no talking.
examples: This chorus has been stuck in my head for a year.

variables.name: song_title
variables.description: Song title, as sung in the chorus

variables.name: chorus_line
variables.description: The single best chorus line, containing the title
variables.example: we wore paper crowns and called it gold

variables.name: story_line
variables.description: One honest sentence about where the song came from
variables.example: Wrote it in my car after my last shift

beats.purpose: hook: chorus already in, title on screen

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 performance shot of {{artist_name}} singing full voice into a vintage mic, single hard spotlight, haze, camera slowly orbiting

beats.purpose: chorus continues with lyric on screen

visual.prompt: Vertical close-up portrait of {{artist_name}}, eyes closed mid-note, warm tungsten light, film grain, lyrics space in lower third
Vertical photo of a parked car at night, notebook and phone on the dashboard, streetlight glow, quiet and real

craft.notes: Start the audio one beat before the chorus downbeat so the first syllable the viewer hears is the title, on a stressed beat 1. Choose the chorus line where the title repeats or sits at the end of the phrase; a line with an internal rhyme (crowns/down, gold/told) gives the ear a second hook. Cut the music to a filtered pad for the spoken story line, then slam back for the release card. Tempo/feel: whatever the song is; the edit works best on 90-130 BPM tracks with a big chorus lift.

do_not: Open with 'Hey guys, new song coming out'
Use an intro or verse; only the strongest chorus line earns the first 3 seconds
Describe the song as sounding like a named famous artist
